title: Mockito Testing
description: Progress from competent JUnit testing to professional Mockito usage — creating mocks, stubbing and verifying behavior, and exercising sound judgment about what to mock — as preparation for Spring Boot service testing.

nodes.label: Mockito Prerequisites
nodes.description: Confirm the Java (classes, interfaces, dependency relationships) and JUnit (@Test, assertions, lifecycle, isolation) prerequisites needed before introducing Mockito.

nodes.label: Why Mockito & Test Doubles
nodes.description: Understand why real dependencies make unit tests slow or difficult, and learn the test-double vocabulary — dummy, stub, fake, mock, and spy — before learning any Mockito annotations.

nodes.label: Creating & Stubbing Mocks
nodes.description: Create mocks with mock(), and stub method return values with when()/thenReturn(), including consecutive results for repeated invocations.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.description: Verify that a mock's method was called with verify(), using count modes like times(), never(), and atLeastOnce(), and understand when interaction verification is preferable to plain state assertions.

nodes.label: Argument Matching & Capturing
nodes.description: Use argument matchers (any(), eq(), argThat()) to stub and verify flexibly, and use ArgumentCaptor to capture and inspect the actual values a collaborator received.

nodes.description: Integrate Mockito with JUnit Jupiter using MockitoExtension, @Mock, and @InjectMocks, and understand exactly how @InjectMocks differs from real Spring dependency injection.

nodes.label: Exceptions & Void Methods
nodes.description: Stub exceptions with thenThrow() to test error-handling paths, and use doNothing()/doThrow()/doAnswer() for void methods where when().thenReturn() doesn't apply.

nodes.label: Custom Answers
nodes.description: Use thenAnswer() to generate dynamic, argument-dependent responses from a mock, keeping custom answers small rather than recreating production logic inside test setup.

nodes.label: Spies & Partial Mocking
nodes.description: Use spy() to wrap a real object and selectively stub behavior, using doReturn().when() to avoid triggering real methods accidentally, and recognize partial mocking as a possible design smell.

nodes.label: Mocking Design Decisions
nodes.description: Identify which dependencies are good candidates for mocking — repositories, external APIs, clocks — and which should almost never be mocked, such as value objects, DTOs, and the class under test itself.

nodes.label: Avoiding Over-Mocking
nodes.description: Recognize the warning signs of over-mocking, prefer testing observable behavior over verifying every internal call, and decide when a real object, a fake, or an actual integration test is the better tool than a mock.
